mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.25%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 8.0% in a 3-month window, it signals economic distress that triggers a flight to quality, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 8.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate a sharp contraction in consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply-side recovery phase (INDPRO growth rate above 0.5% monthly), manufacturing output expansion supports corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% monthly.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate above 1.0% signals robust economic expansion, supporting equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 1.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When monthly payroll growth falls below 50,000 jobs, it signals labor market weakness that reduces consumer spending and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when PAYEMS growth is below 50,000.

mechanism_narrative: When the annualized CPI inflation rate exceeds 3.0%, it signals persistent inflation that prompts central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL annualized inflation exceeds 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%), the central bank's delayed response to inflation causes equity market volatility, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annualized and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%.
